paragraphs.title: Turning to God and Answering the Accusation

easy.explanation: The psalm is written concerning the words of Cush the Benjamite.
easy.q: Who is mentioned as the background of the song?

easy.explanation: David says, “O LORD my God, in thee do I put my trust.”
easy.q: In whom does David put his trust?

easy.explanation: David asks the LORD to save and deliver him from all his persecutors.
easy.q: From what does David ask to be delivered?

answers: To answer the accusation against him
medium.explanation: He declares that he has not done iniquity or repaid evil to a peaceful friend.
medium.q: Why does David declare his innocence?

answers: He released his enemy without cause
medium.explanation: David says that if he released an enemy who had no cause against him, he accepts the consequences.
medium.q: What does David mean by, “I have delivered him that without cause is mine enemy”?

answers: The enemy may persecute and overtake him
medium.explanation: He allows the enemy to persecute him, tread down his life, and lay his honour in the dust.
medium.q: What does David allow to happen if he has done evil?

answers: He asks for rescue while admitting guilt
He asks for rescue while presenting his integrity
He does not address the accusation
challenge.explanation: David asks the LORD for help while declaring that he has not committed the wrong of which he is accused.
challenge.q: What is the connection between David’s request for rescue and his claim of innocence?

challenge.explanation: The lion image portrays a violent danger that could tear David’s soul apart when no deliverer is present.
challenge.q: What does the image of the lion emphasize about David’s persecutor?

answers: If the LORD will not judge the nations
If David has truly done iniquity
challenge.explanation: David says that if he has done the alleged wrong, he accepts the punishment described.
challenge.q: What is the main condition David states in these verses?

easy.explanation: David asks the LORD to rise against his enemies and awaken to judgment.
easy.q: Why does David call on the LORD to arise?

easy.explanation: David says, “So shall the congregation of the people compass thee about.”
easy.q: Who surrounds the LORD in David’s description?

easy.explanation: He asks the LORD to judge him according to his righteousness and integrity.
easy.q: According to what does David ask to be judged?

answers: He asks for judgment to be canceled
He asks to be judged fairly as well
He asks the nations to judge him
medium.explanation: After calling for judgment, David asks the LORD to judge him according to his righteousness and integrity.
medium.q: What is the connection between David’s call for judgment and his personal request?

medium.explanation: The phrase pictures the LORD returning to the high or exalted place after judgment.
medium.q: What does “return thou on high” mean in context?

answers: A call for judgment, the surrounding peoples, and a personal plea
medium.explanation: David calls for judgment, describes the congregation surrounding the LORD, and then asks for personal judgment.
medium.q: What is the sequence of ideas in these verses?

answers: He wants judgment based on his conduct
He wants his enemies to judge him
challenge.explanation: David asks the LORD to examine his actions and integrity.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from David’s request to be judged according to his righteousness?

answers: Judgment is presented as a moral examination
Judgment is presented as a celebration
challenge.explanation: David connects judgment with an examination of his righteousness and integrity.
challenge.q: What does the combination of “judgment” and “my righteousness” suggest?

challenge.explanation: The congregation appears as part of the scene surrounding the LORD in judgment.
challenge.q: What role does the congregation of the peoples have in the description?

paragraphs.title: God Examines Hearts and Protects the Upright

answers: That it come to an end
easy.explanation: David says, “Oh let the wickedness of the wicked come to an end.”
easy.q: What does David ask to happen to the wickedness of the wicked?

easy.explanation: The psalm says that God saves the upright in heart.
The verse says that God is angry with the wicked every day.
easy.q: With whom is God angry every day?

answers: He examines a person’s inner being
medium.explanation: The phrase means that God examines the heart and the inward thoughts.
medium.q: What does “trieth the hearts and reins” mean?

answers: God knows the inner person and saves the upright
God does not know who is upright
medium.explanation: The verses present God as one who examines inward character and saves those who are upright in heart.
medium.q: What is the connection between examining hearts and protecting the upright?
What does David ask after the wickedness of the wicked comes to an end?

answers: Wickedness ends while the just are established
There is no difference between them
challenge.explanation: David asks for wickedness to end and for the just to be established.
challenge.q: What moral principle appears in the contrast between the wicked and the just?

answers: His anger is continual, not merely occasional
His anger existed only in the past
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the continuing nature of God’s anger against the wicked.
challenge.q: What does “every day” teach about God’s attitude toward the wicked?

answers: God judges and protects according to His examination of hearts
challenge.explanation: God is portrayed as the examiner and judge who saves the upright in heart.
challenge.q: How do judgment and protection work together in these verses?

paragraphs.title: The Preparation of Judgment and the Wicked One’s Self-Destruction

answers: The instruments of judgment will be prepared against him
easy.explanation: If he does not turn, the sword, bow, and arrows are made ready against him.
easy.q: What will happen if the wicked person does not turn?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “He made a pit, and digged it.”
easy.q: What does the wicked person dig?

easy.explanation: His violent dealing comes down upon his own pate, or head.
easy.q: Where does the wicked person’s violence come down?

answers: If he does not turn from his way
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to refusing to turn away from the wicked way.
medium.q: What does “if he turn not” mean?

answers: His plan leads to harm from his own actions
medium.explanation: The wicked person prepares mischief but falls into the pit he made.
medium.q: What is the connection between the wicked person’s plan and the pit?

answers: Iniquity, mischief, and falsehood, followed by falling into a pit
medium.explanation: The wicked person conceives wrongdoing and falsehood, then falls into his own ditch.
medium.q: What sequence is described in these verses?

answers: His evil actions return to harm him
challenge.explanation: The image shows the wicked person being harmed by the destructive plan he created.
challenge.q: What does the image of falling into the pit he made mean?

answers: Both portray prepared judgment and the consequences of wickedness
Both symbolize protection for the wicked
challenge.explanation: The passage first describes instruments of judgment and then shows the wicked suffering the result of his own actions.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the weapons and the pit?

answers: Punishment returns directly to the one who committed the violence
The violence remains only with the victim
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes that the wrongdoer’s violence returns upon him.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the violence coming down upon the wicked person’s own head?

easy.explanation: David says, “I will praise the LORD according to his righteousness.”
easy.q: For what does David praise the LORD?

answers: The name of the LORD most high
easy.explanation: David will sing praise to the name of the LORD most high.
easy.q: To whose name will David sing praise?

easy.explanation: The final verse ends with praise to the LORD and singing to His name.

medium.explanation: David praises the LORD in recognition of His righteous character and actions.
medium.q: What does “according to his righteousness” mean?

answers: After describing judgment, David praises the LORD’s righteousness
The ending concerns only the enemies
medium.explanation: The praise concludes the psalm by affirming trust in the LORD’s righteous judgment.
medium.q: What is the connection between the ending and the theme of judgment?

answers: It moves from petition and danger to praise and thanksgiving
It moves from praise to pursuit
It moves from singing to silence
medium.explanation: The psalm closes by moving from requests and danger to praise and thanksgiving.
medium.q: What change occurs at the end of the psalm?

answers: He recognizes the LORD’s righteousness and judgment
challenge.explanation: Praising the LORD’s righteousness shows David’s trust in His just judgment.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from David’s praise after describing judgment?

answers: It expresses public worship of the LORD’s name
challenge.explanation: Singing praise to the name of the Most High expresses open worship and thanksgiving.
challenge.q: How does singing strengthen the meaning of David’s praise?

challenge.explanation: The psalm ends with praise according to the LORD’s righteousness.
challenge.q: Which idea from the psalm is summarized in the final verse?
